zh.earthSky: 地面夜空示意 · 银河光带
zh.observer: 观察位置 · 移动的是镜头
zh.skyHint: 切换视线，再移动观察位置；滚轮或双指可缩放。
zh.orionHint: 拖动左右或移动观察位置；点星星可读距离，方向键也可移动。
zh.systemHint: 轨道共用AU尺；拖动旋转，滚轮或双指缩放。
zh.skyBoundary: 银河结构与星光投影示意 · 非实时星图，未命名星点不是实测目录。
zh.orionBoundary: J2000方向与2007视差示例 · 星点是定位符，距离估计有不确定性。
zh.systemBoundary: 轨道半径共尺 · 天体定位球放大，表面是假想插画；并排中心仅为排版。
zh.diskCue: 沿着薄盘看，视线穿过较多星光，尘埃形成暗带。地面夜空可单独切换。
zh.poleCue: 朝盘外看，银河光带退开了，稀疏的恒星仍然可见。
zh.andromedaCue: 认星连线中的星在银河内；小光斑M31是远处的整座星系。
zh.outsideCue: 金环始终是太阳的位置。视线从盘内出发，朝向刚才那片天空。
zh.orionCue: 看着像平面图，实际有远有近。先猜猜腰带三颗星是否一样远。
zh.depthCue: 星星没有移动，是我们换了观察位置；虚线是视线，不是连接恒星的绳子。
zh.range: 视差形式误差所对应的范围
zh.estimateNote: 采用2007视差倒数示例；亮星、多星另有不同测距结果，范围不含所有系统误差。
zh.patternNote: 连线帮助认图，不表示物理连接或整座星系。
zh.solarLabel: 太阳系内侧 · 这里只画水星
zh.mercuryOutside: 水星轨道在近景之外 · 0.387 AU
zh.planetCue: 七颗行星都在水星轨道的内侧。近景仍保留同一AU单位。
zh.keplerLink: 还有绕着双恒星转的行星 →
zh.m31Boundary: 目录方向定位 · M31光斑放大以便辨认，不与银河盘共用距离比例。
zh.orionRegion: 猎户座这七颗星 · 太阳附近
zh.orionContextBoundary: 背景为结构示意；青色点是七颗指定亮星的估计位置，定位圈和点均不表示直径。
zh.groundHint: 先看地面夜空，再切换「沿盘面看」观察银河结构。
zh.groundBoundary: 地面夜空与地形为示意，非实拍或实时星图；未命名星点不是实测目录。
zh.groundCue: 银河是地面夜空中的光带。切换「沿盘面看」，再观察这条视线怎样穿过银河薄盘。
zh.wholeCue: 太阳系里有木星、土星这样的巨行星。另一边是红矮星和七颗较小的岩质行星；点选看看，再用同尺对照它们的轨道。
zh.wholeBoundary: 全貌将轨道展开，定位球放大，不用于量距；TRAPPIST-1表面为假想插画。绕行采用圆形轨道近似。
zh.wholeLayout: 轨道展开示意 · 不共用距离标尺
zh.wholeHint: 两个完整行星系统，轨道展开便于识别；可转动、点选、播放或切到共同AU尺。

en.earthSky: Illustrative sky from Earth · Milky Way band
en.foreground: Foreground stars in the Milky Way
en.m31Button: Follow this sightline to M31’s structure →
en.bridgeButton: Is this the Milky Way in our sky? →
en.skyHint: Change the sightline, then move the observer. Wheel or pinch to magnify.
en.orionHint: Drag sideways or move the observer. Select stars for distances; arrow keys work too.
en.systemHint: Orbits share an AU ruler. Drag to rotate; wheel or pinch to magnify.
en.skyBoundary: Illustrative Galactic structure and starlight projection · not a live sky chart; unnamed dots are not surveyed stars.
en.orionBoundary: J2000 directions with selected 2007 parallaxes · dots are locators; distances are uncertain.
en.systemBoundary: One orbital scale · body symbols are enlarged and surfaces hypothetical; side-by-side centres are layout only.
en.diskCue: Along the thin disk, more starlight accumulates and dust makes dark lanes. The Earth-sky view has its own switch.
en.poleCue: Away from the disk, the bright band leaves our view, but scattered stars remain visible.
en.andromedaCue: Pattern stars are in our Milky Way; the small M31 smudge is a whole distant galaxy.
en.outsideCue: The gold ring keeps the Sun’s position. Its sightline points toward the sky we just saw.
en.orionCue: It looks like a flat pattern, but stars lie at different depths. Are the three belt stars equally distant?
en.depthCue: The stars stayed still while we moved. Dashed rays are sightlines, not strings joining stars.
en.range: Range from the formal parallax error
en.estimateNote: Uses a reciprocal 2007 parallax; other bright/multiple-star distance estimates differ. Bars omit possible systematic errors.
en.patternNote: Pattern lines aid recognition; they are not physical links or a whole galaxy.
en.mercuryOutside: Mercury’s orbit is outside this close-up · 0.387 AU
en.planetCue: All seven lie inside Mercury’s orbit. The close-up retains the same AU unit.
en.keplerLink: Planets can also orbit two stars →
en.m31Boundary: Catalogued direction · M31’s patch is enlarged for recognition, without the Galactic disk’s distance scale.
en.orionWhere: Where are these stars in our galaxy?
en.orionRegion: These seven Orion stars · near the Sun
en.orionContextBoundary: Background is structural illustration; cyan locators mark seven selected stellar position estimates, not body diameters.
en.groundHint: Look at the ground-level night sky, then choose Along the disk to examine Galactic structure.
en.groundBoundary: Illustrative night sky and ground, not a photograph or live sky chart; unnamed dots are not surveyed stars.
en.groundCue: The Milky Way appears as a band in the night sky. Choose Along the disk to see how that sightline crosses our Galactic disk.
en.wholeCue: Our family includes giants such as Jupiter and Saturn. The other contains a red dwarf and seven smaller rocky planets. Select members, then compare their orbits on the same ruler.
en.wholeBoundary: Whole views spread the orbits and enlarge body markers, without a distance ruler. TRAPPIST-1 surfaces are hypothetical; motion uses circular-orbit approximations.
en.wholeLayout: Spread orbital layout · no shared distance scale
en.wholeHint: Two complete planetary families with spread orbits. Turn, select members, play or switch to a common AU ruler.
en.mapCredit: Solar maps: Solar System Scope · CC BY 4.0
